title: China-to-Serbia EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Connector Redesign — IEC 62196 Type 2 and CCS2
rows.target_requirement: Serbia follows a European EV interface ecosystem in most commercial charging programs. IEC 62196 Type 2 is typically used for AC charging, while CCS Combo 2 is commonly used for DC fast charging when specified by the operator, fleet, or public tender. Connector selection is a technical interoperability and procurement requirement, not direct proof that the whole charger is legally approved.
target_standards: Project, fleet, operator, or public-procurement connector requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China-market evidence commonly uses GB/T 20234.2 for AC charging connection devices and GB/T 20234.3 for DC charging interfaces, with GB/T 27930 for charger-to-vehicle communication. GB/T hardware and signalling should not be presented as Type 2 or CCS2 conformity without connector, cable, locking, pilot, communication, labels, and safety re-evaluation.
rows.gap: GB/T-first chargers need a hardware and protocol conversion plan for Serbia-facing projects: Type 2 or CCS2 couplers, cable thermal rating, lock and proximity circuits, control-pilot behavior, DC PLC communication where CCS2 is used, labels, spare-part list, and retesting after connector redesign.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where the intended Serbia deployment, procurement document, charging network, or vehicle fleet specifies Type 2 / CCS2; otherwise a market-interoperability expectation rather than a standalone legal approval
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 20234 conformity is a China-market connector baseline and is not a substitute for Type 2 or CCS2 compatibility

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not describe a GB/T 20234 connector package as Serbia Type 2 or CCS2 ready. Connector hardware, communication, labels, and safety evidence should be rebuilt around the intended IEC interface for the Serbia deployment.

rows.target_requirement: Serbian EV charging projects typically require site and charging-service review through AERS and EMS procedures when connected to public networks or grid-connected assets. This includes power interconnection, protection settings, remote monitoring interfaces, metering logic, energization, commissioning, and tariff/compliance reporting.
target_standards: AERS charging-site and grid-connection obligations where applicable
EMS distribution-level connection and acceptance requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China chargers may include GB/T 18487 reports and domestic dispatch-site review documents. These are useful for technical mapping, but they do not replace Serbian AERS or EMS site connection obligations for charging assets.
china_standards: China charging network approval and dispatch procedures where applicable
rows.gap: The gap is Serbia project approval context. Exporters should provide EMS route mapping, site electrical project files, grid studies, protection matrices, telemetry plan, commissioning logs, ownership of operation responsibilities, and Serbian-language acceptance checklists.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for projects requiring charging-network connection and EMS acceptance; often mandatory in public or utility-linked deployments
mandatory_status.cn: China project acceptance documents do not transfer to Serbian grid or service operation rights

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not treat EV charger grid-test evidence as a full Serbian market decision. Confirm AERS route, EMS project connection path, and operator acceptance evidence before commissioning.

source.publisher: Energy Agency of the Republic of Serbia (AERS)

rows.target_requirement: Serbia is EU-candidate and aligns CE-oriented product legislation for many electrical and electronic goods in the EU model. EV chargers should be screened for LVD, EMC, and RED scope by model and function, with mandatory documentation for installation, manuals, risk analysis, marking, declaration of conformity, and any required local language content.
target_standards: Directive 2014/35/EU Low Voltage Directive, where voltage scope applies
Directive 2014/53/EU Radio Equipment Directive, where radio equipment is included
Serbia market-placement practice for EV charging infrastructure
rows.china_equivalent: China GB charger evidence, including GB/T 18487.1 and related series, supports technical review and can help map clauses. However, this evidence is not a direct authorization for Serbia market placement, including AERS operator and local operator requirements.
rows.gap: The gap is market-placement documentation rather than only electrical test performance. Exporters should map each SKU to LVD, EMC, RED, RoHS and Serbia EU-oriented expectations, and prepare conformity files, marking, manuals, risk assessment, installer and operator acceptance documents.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where the charger is within Serbia CE-oriented scope requiring market-placement documentation; RED applies when radio modules are integrated
mandatory_status.cn: China GB/T evidence does not authorize Serbia market placement or operator acceptance

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat Serbia CE-oriented scope screening as a market-placement gate for EV chargers. LVD, EMC, and RED application must be model- and function-specific.

source.publisher: EUR-Lex / EC-Turkey model references and Serbia market integration guidance

rows.target_requirement: EV chargers for Serbia-facing projects often need OCPP interoperability with operators and backend systems. OCPP 1.6, OCPP 2.0.1, and OCPP 2.1 versions are commonly referenced, while security profile, transport method, and EMS-facing workflow requirements should be confirmed before launch. OCPP is not a standalone product safety certification route.
rows.china_equivalent: GB/T 27930 is commonly used for China charger-to-vehicle communication, but it is a vehicle-interface protocol and does not replace OCPP backend interoperability, cybersecurity profiles, remote-management tests, or operator acceptance.
rows.gap: The Serbia target package should identify OCPP version, security profile, certificate handling, meter-value mapping, transaction model, remote reset and firmware processes, communications architecture, and test evidence from the assigned operator backend.

mandatory_status.target: Usually mandatory when required by operator, tender, data-sharing, roaming, payment, or maintenance specification; OCPP is not itself a whole-unit safety certification
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 27930 is vehicle-side communication and does not satisfy backend OCPP requirements

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm OCPP version and security profile with the Serbia operator before shipment. GB/T 27930 support does not prove backend interoperability with EMS-facing or operator-facing charging management systems.

rows.requirement: EMC, Low-Voltage Safety, and Residual-Current Protection
rows.target_requirement: Serbian EV chargers placed on the market normally need conformity evidence for applicable electrical safety and electromagnetic compatibility legislation. IEC 61851-1 includes EVSE electrical-safety requirements, while EMC evidence is mapped separately to applicable EMC routes and charger-specific EMC test standards. Residual-current protection, DC residual-current detection, protective earthing, overcurrent protection, surge protection, and installation coordination should be documented for the final site design.
target_standards: Directive 2014/35/EU Low Voltage Directive, Serbia implementation to be verified
Directive 2014/30/EU EMC Directive, Serbia implementation to be verified
IEC 61851-21-2 EMC route for off-board EV charging systems
rows.china_equivalent: China files may include GB/T 18487.1 safety evidence, GB/T 18487.2 EMC evidence for off-board conductive supply equipment, component certificates, and site electrical drawings. These should be clause-mapped and retested where needed for Serbia CE-aligned practice, system earthing, RCD design, and installation assumptions.
rows.gap: The gap is often in installation assumptions rather than lab reports only: earthing system, upstream breaker, RCD type or RDC-DD arrangement, DC leakage handling, EMC cable routing, surge protection, short-circuit rating, enclosure IP/IK, ambient rating, and Serbian-language warnings should match the actual deployment.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where applicable CE-aligned low-voltage and EMC legislation applies; RCD and installation protections are mandatory where required by the applicable installation design, grid connection, or electrical code route
mandatory_status.cn: China GB/T safety and EMC evidence supports comparison but does not replace Serbia CE and site-installation verification

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not rely on a China EMC or safety report without checking Serbia CE scope, IEC / EN test coverage, and the real site protection design. Residual-current protection, earthing, leakage detection, and EMC installation assumptions should be validated before commissioning.
